picks.why: True capsule proportions with a small docking collar at the top. It reads as a capsule at once, while 1 is a squat, blunt cone.
The tail streams naturally behind the ice body, so it reads as a comet. In 2 the tail hooks around and ends in a glowing spark, which is an invented extra.
The cleanest rock: simple craters and modest crystal clusters, without the heavy crack lines of 1 and 2. It has the calm, simple modelling of the real cards.
One orbit ring keeps the extras lowest and the object reads as a globe on a stand. 1 and 3 tangle two crossing rings over the sphere.
Best balance of tube and cap, with a natural crumpled foil body and a slim bendy straw. 2 leans awkwardly, and the plain white straw in 1 is flatter.
Only candidate. It reads instantly as a glowing alien plant in a pot and has a clean, simple silhouette.

Separate constellations with a true star shape read instantly as a star chart, and the sheet curls naturally. 2 joins its shapes into a network, and the star in 3 is a soft outline on a more oddly cut sheet.
Fills the frame the way real cards do, with a simple ring and a clear module and panel layout. 2 is smaller, with busier spokes and end hardware.

The yellow pad marking makes the launch pad read instantly, and the rocket and slim tower are balanced. In 1 the tower is too heavy, and 2 has a plain pad with a bright yellow railing that draws the eye.
Clean dome with no invented spire or finial, solid building proportions and a telescope that clearly reads through the slit. It is the most restrained of the three, like the real cards.
